title: introduce-schema-retention-proxy-and-stream-sanitize-adapter
author: Jinwoo Park
release_notes: Adds a runtime proxy that retains request schema preferences, a beta header for schema negotiation, and a stream sanitizer to stabilize legacy client streams. Backwards-compatible by default; opt-in beta required for schema coercion.
description:
Summary: Introduces a lightweight request-side compatibility proxy (Schema Retention Proxy) and a Stream Sanitizer adapter to improve stability for legacy clients during schema rollouts. Motivated by recent regressions when clients and server disagree on the response envelope (structured output vs. raw text) and by intermittent streaming deserialization errors from older SDKs. This PR provides a conservative, opt-in path (X-Redwood-Schema-Beta header) to enable server-side coercion and sanitization while preserving default backward compatibility for clients that do not opt in.

What changed: 1) schema-retention-proxy: runtime middleware that records client-declared preferences (schema-version, prefer-structured) and attaches a compact capability token to requests hitting the model-serving layer. The token allows downstream components to apply targeted coercion rules instead of global rewrites. 2) stream-sanitizer: an interceptor for streaming responses that normalizes control frames (tool call markers, chunked JSON fragments) and emits consistent chunk boundaries for older clients. 3) response-coercer: a small, deterministic mapper that converts structured tool-call envelopes to legacy tool-call proto when the client indicates prefer=legacy via header or capability token. 4) tests and integration harness updates for OpenAI-compat layer to exercise mixed-version client/server scenarios.

Motivation and rationale: During staged schema rollouts we observed two primary failure modes: a) older SDKs choke on interleaved structured-JSON fragments in a stream and b) clients that assume legacy tool-call envelopes received unexpected fields leading to deserialization exceptions. Our strategy is to avoid hard breakages by keeping the default path untouched and offering an opt-in beta header that signals a client is prepared to receive coerced responses and streaming frames. The proxy also enables telemetry on negotiation failures to guide future migrations.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc: ENG-4192 linked - [x] Unit tests for proxy and coercer - [x] Integration tests: legacy SDK streaming test matrix - [x] E2E perf smoke to ensure <5% p95 latency regression - [x] Docs: Console and SDK notes (beta header usage) - [x] Add rollout plan and feature flag gating for 2-week canary

Commits (high-level): - a1b2c3: add schema-retention-proxy middleware and capability token format - b2c3d4: implement stream-sanitizer interceptor and chunk normalizer - c3d4e5: add response-coercer for tool-call envelopes with unit tests - d4e5f6: integration tests for mixed-version clients + harness updates - e5f6a7: docs and changelog entries; add feature flag and canary config

Files changed (high-level): - runtime/middleware/schema_retention_proxy.go: new middleware and token encoding - runtime/streaming/stream_sanitizer.go: interceptor that normalizes stream frames and drops invalid fragments for non-opt-in clients - runtime/response/coercer.go: deterministic map from v2 structured-tool to v1 legacy envelope - sdk/openai_compat/fixtures/: test clients and recorded streams for matrix - docs/platform/schema_rollout.md: beta header docs and migration guidance - tests/integration/legacy_stream_matrix.test: new integration scenarios - ci/rollout-config.yaml: canary policy for feature flag

Review conversation (excerpted): - Sofia Martinez (reviewer): "Thanks, overall this looks like a safe approach. Can we make the capability token size bounded to avoid header bloat for high-FPS clients?" - Author (Jinwoo): "Token is a 12-byte base64 blob; added a test to ensure header length <150 bytes for worst-case metadata." - Ravi Shah: "Stream sanitizer looks good, but we should avoid dropping frames silently; add a metric and a debug log line so SREs can triage." - Author: "Added sanitized_frame_drop_total histogram and debug logging behind debug flag." - Maya Thompson: "Docs callout: emphasize that beta header is required for coercion; otherwise behavior is unchanged. Also include suggested SDK upgrade notes." - Author: "Updated docs and changelog per suggestion."

CI: Initial run (linux-unit, integration, lint) showed a flaky integration failure around streaming timeouts (integration/legacy_stream_matrix.test). Root cause was an undersized context timeout in the harness for legacy clients; increased timeout and retried CI. Reran full pipeline: all checks passed (linux-unit: pass, integration: pass, lint: pass, e2e-smoke: pass).

Telemetry and rollout: Feature gated behind runtime feature flag runtime.enable_schema_coercion (disabled by default). Beta header X-Redwood-Schema-Beta: true opt-in required to enable coercion and the stream sanitizer's aggressive fixes. We will enable the feature flag for 2% of requests in staging for one week, then 10% in prod for a canary cohort before wider rollout. Telemetry added: negotiation_failure_count, sanitized_frame_drop_total, schema_coercion_applied_count.

Backward compatibility notes: Default behavior for clients that do not set X-Redwood-Schema-Beta is unchanged. The proxy only records metadata and will not modify responses unless the token indicates an opt-in or the feature flag is enabled for the specific request. This minimizes risk while allowing safe testing.

Release notes (user-facing): Adds an opt-in beta header (X-Redwood-Schema-Beta) to enable structured output negotiation and server-side stream sanitization for SDKs that opt into the new schema. No action required for most customers. SDK maintainers: see docs for migration/test suites.

Merge: After two approvals (Sofia Martinez, Ravi Shah) and a successful CI rerun, the branch was squashed and merged to main (squash merge). Merge commit: d3f7a1c9.

Follow-ups: - ENG-4192.1: add SDK helpers to emit capability tokens automatically - ENG-4192.2: observability dashboard tile for negotiation failures - PM-1299: schedule customer announcement if canary metrics remain stable
